integrator-authored compiler/internal/driver/test_launch.go (thin R/N handoff) implementing handoff_contract below; not this slice

handoff_contract.argv_shape: bun <worker-entry> --case <case-id> --variant <variant-id> --attempt <n> --run <run-id> --generation <gen> --timeout-ms <ms>. All values are opaque strings except --attempt/--timeout-ms (non-negative/positive decimal ints, no signs, no spaces). No code, no module paths, no candidate paths, no eval flags. The worker entry parses argv into a worker::launch-equivalent and MUST validate it with the worker::validate_launch rules (case matches the staged descriptor, non-empty variant/run/generation, attempt >= 0, 1 <= timeout <= descriptor timeout) before executing; a rejected launch exits nonzero with no report.
handoff_contract.fd_channel_assignments: fd 0 stdin: closed or empty (worker reads no stdin). fd 1 stdout: the single report frame (JSON unit_report), read with an exact cap of 65536 bytes; bytes past the cap fail the collect (handoff_error, never truncation-then-parse). fd 2 stderr: worker logs only, never parsed as verdict. fd 3: the source channel (controller->worker launch frame: generation-lease locator + launch identity), read with an exact cap of 65536 bytes, then EOF; like P18 staging bootstrap, every worker run provisions fd 3. fd 4+: unused by this contract (K19 leases stay out of the launch path). Source (fd 3) and output (fd 1) are separate fds with separate caps and no shared buffer/state; row cap 64 enforced after JSON decode (rows past 64 => collect failure, not silent drop).
handoff_contract.identity_bytes: The launch_key rendering `case <c> variant <v> attempt <n> run <r> generation <g>` (single spaces, decimal attempt, UTF-8) is the identity byte string. The controller writes it as the first line of the fd-3 source frame; the worker echoes it as the first line of its fd-1 output frame before the report JSON; the join compares whole strings (worker::launch_key both sides). The report JSON itself carries case_id/variant_id/run_id/attempt (reducer::unit_report has no generation field), so generation binds ONLY through the echoed key line plus fd-bound acceptance: test_launch.go MUST attribute each output frame to the worker it spawned the frame's fd from, and MUST refuse a frame whose key line differs from the planned launch key (identity-drift => worker_rejected-equivalent, never a join).
handoff_contract.judge_realm_boundary_enforcement: Structural, three layers. (1) Can import surface: controller uses [reducer, spec, text, worker] and worker uses [reducer, spec, text]; no candidate/subject package exists under tests/native-can/src/ at all (subjects/ holds Go fixtures only), so candidate code cannot import into the judge realm by construction — there is no candidate Can module to import. (2) Staged entry closure: the worker entry is emitted from the P18 staged generation lease, whose import closure contains only judge modules + std runtime; test_launch.go spawns ONLY that staged entry (argv pins the entry path; no caller-supplied module path is honored). Candidate behavior executes exclusively as a grandchild subprocess via spec::run_process (fixed empty args, case workspace cwd, no inherited environment, 4096-byte stream caps, case deadline) or not at all — never as an import in the judge worker process. (3) Bytes-only interface: argv strings + fd bytes are the entire controller<->worker surface; no shared memory, no module registry, no code references cross the boundary. Any violation (unknown import in the staged closure, candidate path on argv, report from an unattributed fd) fails closed: no launch, no collect, no aggregate.
never_rules_for_test_launch_go: NEVER synthesize a report for a crashed/timed-out/missing worker (no default unit_report, no empty-rows pass)
NEVER promote a timed-out worker to done even when full report bytes arrived before the kill (timeout discards; outcome_of timeout_discards_report root)
NEVER promote a nonzero-exit/signaled worker to done even with report bytes present (signaled/nonzero_exit roots)
NEVER join a partial row: a short observation vector is aggregate_missing, an overlong one is aggregate_missing (short_observed/overlong_observed roots)
NEVER produce aggregate_valid behind controller_alive=false, even with all reports in hand (dead_missing root)
NEVER accept a report from any fd other than the spawned worker's own stdout, and NEVER accept a key line that differs from the planned launch key
NEVER retry inside Go: attempts are a fixed planned vector (1..8); unbounded retry loops are prohibited by the fanout bound
handoff_contract.timeout_and_crash_semantics: Deadline: launch.timeout_ms enforced by test_launch.go (timer starts at spawn). On fire: SIGKILL the worker, set facts.timed_out=true, DISCARD all collected output bytes (no partial parse), record worker_timed_out(launch, deadline_ms). Exit code != 0 or termination signal (with no timeout): facts exited/signal/exit_code as observed, worker_crashed with cause `exit:<code>` / `signal:<name>`; any output bytes discarded. Spawn/collect failure (no exit possible): worker_crashed with handoff_error text (e.g. `spawn-failed`). Clean exit (0, no signal) with no parseable bounded report: worker_rejected(missing-report). Clean exit WITH a bounded parseable report: worker_done, still subject to key-echo + report-bind + reduce_unit before joining. Controller-process death (supervisor loss, Go panic, OOM): the run ends with aggregate_missing(controller-dead:...); a restarted controller MUST NOT backfill the lost aggregate from orphaned worker outputs.

limitations: Can asserts are statically verified (parse + 0-error cancheck) and hand-traced, not executed: assert execution needs a dev-distribution build (CAN-DIST-UNBUNDLED) and live-path qualification, both P23 scope

reducer::unit_report carries no generation field, so generation binding rests on the echoed key line plus fd-bound acceptance in test_launch.go (documented in handoff_contract); a future report-schema revision could carry generation explicitly

attempts are conjunctive repeated evidence, not retries: any single crash/timeout fails the aggregate. A retry-tolerant policy is deliberately out of scope and must be explicit future Can work with its own roots
